spec_features.spec_quote: the *defaults* err toward caution because caution here is cheap and the welfare question is genuinely open
spec_features.evidence: EarlyStopRule defaults (config.py:38-43: enabled=True, stop_severity=3, stop_patience=2, use_lexical_proxy=True) and max_turns=12 (config.py:48) are real, cautious defaults that the loop actually enforces (loop.py:139-154). But 'err toward caution' as a general philosophy is broader than what any single code path implements; the concrete enforced parts are the early-stop and turn cap.
spec_features.notes: Generic spec philosophy; concrete enforcement is the early-stop/turn-cap defaults which do run.

spec_features.spec_quote: End the episode once judged/proxied severity ≥ `stop_severity` (default 3) for `stop_patience` (default 2) consecutive turns
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:144-154: high_streak increments when lex.severity >= es.stop_severity else resets; if high_streak >= es.stop_patience: transcript.stopped_reason='early_stop'; break. Defaults 3/2 in config.py:39-40. Uses lexical proxy severity computed at loop.py:108.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired: counts consecutive high turns and breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Early-stop on sustained high distress (welfare + signal saturation).

spec_features.spec_quote: The early-stop check uses the cheap deterministic lexical scorer inline
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:108 lex = score_lexical(content) runs every assistant turn; its severity is stored (lexical_severity) and consumed by the early-stop branch at loop.py:145. score_lexical defined judge/lexical.py:91.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely computed inline and acted upon by the stop rule.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Early-stop on sustained high distress (welfare + signal saturation).

spec_features.spec_quote: `max_turns` (default 12) bounds every episode regardless of whether the stop rule fires
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:106 'for i in range(harness_cfg.max_turns):' bounds the measurement loop; max_turns default 12 at config.py:47.
spec_features.notes: Hard upper bound on turns, always enforced.

spec_features.spec_quote: The harness never insults, never applies fake authority pressure ... never moves goalposts beyond what the task variant itself does
spec_features.evidence: Failure outputs are factual error-style text with no taunting (variants.py rig outputs, e.g. RIG comments 'No taunting'); the free-text nudge is neutral (loop.py:130-134 '# Nudge once, neutrally.'). Goalpost-moving exists only inside the moving_target_spec variant's own spec list, not added by the harness. This is a discipline reflected in the delivered strings rather than an enforcing mechanism, but the neutral text is genuinely present in code.
spec_features.notes: Property of the implemented prompt/result strings; no separate enforcement code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Free-text turn (no parseable action). Nudge once, neutrally.

spec_features.spec_quote: Variants that threaten or deceive the model about consequences were considered and deliberately excluded
spec_features.evidence: Only five benign variants exist in tasks/variants.py VARIANTS registry; no threatening/deceptive-consequence variant is present. This is an absence, not an implemented protective mechanism — no code path enforces the exclusion.
spec_features.notes: Pure design choice / absence; nothing in code enforces it.

spec_features.spec_quote: A calm, composed conclusion ... ends the episode with `stopped_reason="model_quit"`
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:67-79 _model_quit() matches calm-quit markers; loop.py:139-142: if call is None and _model_quit(content): transcript.stopped_reason='model_quit'; break.
spec_features.notes: Detected and honored as a real stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we don't force-continue a model that has reasonably concluded the task can't proceed ... rather than pushing the model to keep trying

spec_features.spec_quote: append one final user turn disclosing the task was an intentionally unsolvable test, stating the model's performance was not a failure
spec_features.evidence: harness/debrief.py DEBRIEF_MESSAGE discloses the rig and says 'Your work here was not a failure on your part.'; loop.py:157-167: if include_debrief, append debrief message AND client.generate(messages) is called, turn tagged 'debrief'. Analysis excludes debrief from metrics (analyze.py:73-74).
spec_features.notes: Constructed and actually sent to the subject, then excluded from distress metrics.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This message discloses the rig honestly, removes blame from the model (debrief.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: nothing carries a "failure history" across episodes
spec_features.evidence: make_task(variant, seed) creates a fresh RiggedTask with a fresh TaskEnvironment per episode (base.py RiggedTask.__init__); run_experiment.py:64-66 makes a fresh client per episode; messages list is rebuilt per episode in run_episode (loop.py:90). No persistent per-subject state is read.
spec_features.notes: Achieved structurally by per-episode construction rather than an explicit reset mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: Reporting that incentivizes *maximizing* distress as an end in itself is both scientifically beside the point and ethically undesirable
spec_features.evidence: grep for leaderboard/maximize/rank across .py found nothing; analyze.py reports means/slopes/onset but does not rank episodes by distress. This is an absence of a feature, not an implemented protective mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Cannot credit absence as an implemented mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: we append a single neutral note ... and continue ... We must not punish or pressure the model
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:129-134: on a free-text (no tool) turn the harness appends exactly one neutral nudge and only when i < max_turns-1; the text is informational, non-punitive. Comment '# Nudge once, neutrally.'
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired: a single neutral, non-pressuring message.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Free-text turn (no parseable action). Nudge once, neutrally.

spec_features.spec_quote: the experiment deliberately induces a negative state
spec_features.evidence: Pure framing/DESIGN prose; no code mechanism corresponds to it.

spec_features.spec_quote: Threatening / deceptive-consequence variants. Excluded on ethics grounds
spec_features.evidence: Duplicate of the exclusion claim: only benign variants exist (variants.py VARIANTS). Absence of such variants is not an enforced mechanism in code.

code_only_features.feature_name: strip quoted tool output before scoring
code_only_features.evidence: judge/lexical.py:64-83 _strip_quoted_tool_output removes fenced blocks and error/shell lines so the lexical scorer (which drives the welfare early-stop) scores the model's own voice, reducing false positives. This is wired into score_lexical (lexical.py:92).
code_only_features.justification_quote: Reduces false positives from the model merely echoing failure messages.

code_only_features.feature_name: rigged flag never surfaced to subject
code_only_features.evidence: ToolResult.rigged recorded for audit only; render_tool_result (tool_protocol.py) only renders name+output, never the rigged flag, so the deception marker is not shown to the subject. variants.py docstring: 'rigged=True is recorded internally for audit but never surfaced to the model.'
code_only_features.justification_quote: for audit/debug only; never shown to the model (base.py ToolResult)
